segments.note: The why retains completeness, consistent structure, downstream purpose, and all listed shape categories; the planner-emission scope remains explicit.

activation.note: Activation covers initial and repeated planner component emissions, including missing-input-parent violations, and excludes edits that emit no component. Task terms are explicitly non-gating hints; missing phase/emission observers are honestly labeled needs_new_observer.

audit.summary: All 46 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with required construction details available to the coder and illustrative source examples retained for verification. The then specifies one complete-component shape contract; there are no undeclared requirements, waivers, shared-node misplacements, or application-specific activation constraints.

segmentChecks.note: The why preserves the completeness and consistent-structure purpose, downstream benefit, planner-emission scope, and all structural categories; omitting an explicit second mention of URN is harmless because the URN obligation is explicit in then.

The coder-facing given/when/then covers generated-component scope and every required element: URN, required parent, templated description, at most three consumed and produced events, and dependencies.
The exact component:{wagon}.{feature}.{business_capability}.{side}.{layer} pattern appears unchanged in then.
Then requires the parent feature to equal the input feature URN, and avoid explicitly states that a missing input URN does not exempt an emitted component.
Then reproduces the complete description template with all three placeholders and rejects free-form descriptions in avoid.
Then retains both ioSeeds sources, role-versus-capability filtering, and the cap of three for each event direction; avoid also rejects unfiltered copies.
Then and avoid preserve both required dependency categories: other components in the same feature and external dependencies.

risks: The coder-facing fields do not explain how a component role or capability maps to individual ioSeeds events, so a weak planner could apply an arbitrary or incorrect relevance filter.
When more than three events survive filtering, no ordering or selection rule is given; a weak planner cannot determine which three to emit.
External dependencies must be included, but their discovery source is unspecified, so a weak planner may omit them or invent them.
The combined then clause is dense, which increases the risk that a weak planner misses one of the several independent shape checks, although all required checks are present.

unobservable: phase=planning requires a new harness/session observer and is not derivable from paths alone.
change=component_generated requires a new planner-output observer capable of distinguishing initial or repeated component emission from unrelated plan edits.
task_term is LLM-judged rather than Datalog-observable, although it is explicitly only a non-gating hint.

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the canonical structure contract, and the sampled destinations support the auditor's PASS. The coder-facing rule is usable for the explicit shape checks but remains ambiguous about event relevance, overflow selection, and external-dependency discovery; applicability is well-defined semantically but not currently evaluable by Datalog without the declared observers.
